limitations: P1 — Theorem5.1 lacks zero-drift restriction — Counterevidence: Both proofs expressly assume VE zero drift; correct VP formula preserves SNR ordering

P1 — Theorem5.1 lacks zero-drift restriction — Alternatives and counterevidence: Both proofs explicitly work under zero drift, so the fault is scope of the theorem rather than the VE calculation. The VP correction multiplies all initial spectral powers by the same factor and retains the claimed high-to-low SNR threshold order when the initial ordering holds. This is not an exact autoregressive generative factorization.
P2 — Upsampling approximation lacks alias-error conditions — Counterevidence: Approximation sign and natural-image high-frequency-small motivation; empirical comparison not refuted

P2 — Upsampling approximation lacks alias-error conditions — Alternatives and counterevidence: Eq12 is explicitly approximate and the zero-fill rationale invokes small high-frequency energy in practice. Therefore this is an unstated error regime/alias qualification, not proof that the approximate algorithm always performs poorly. The released comparison uses bicubic downsampling, so its FID need not test the theorem's average-pooling premise.
